## Why visit

A strong beer-focused stop on the station-to-centre approach, offering changing cask alongside a substantial modern bottle and keg selection. It is useful when you want variety beyond one brewery’s range and can add a cider without changing venue. The atmosphere is more contemporary and sometimes livelier than Chester’s traditional pubs, with sport on screens; choose the timing accordingly. It works particularly well as a later stop after food at Harkers or a heritage visit in the centre. Look at the live board for current stock, while treating it as a momentary snapshot.

## Beer

CAMRA’s October 2026 update records six cask handpumps, mainly changing micros, with Landlord as a regular, plus keg/bottles/cans.

## Cider and perry

**Real cider documented; reconfirm stock.** CAMRA documents two real ciders regularly available; ask for current products.

## Food

CAMRA lists pizza, mezze and meat/cheese platters; check the current menu and kitchen.

## Plan the visit

Official site lists later opening on Monday–Thursday than at weekends. Sport can change the noise level; live music has moved to its sister venue.

**Getting there:** City Road, walkable from Chester station.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
